status: Research map · no demonstrated expectation gap
purpose: Trace a completed agent task through resources consumed, the supplier's actual paid unit, incremental cash, and market expectations. A category's growth is not a company or stock conclusion.

gates.label: 1 · Incremental work
gates.detail: Is the task or resource use new, rather than a displaced human or digital channel?

gates.label: 2 · Supplier cash
gates.detail: Does paid usage survive allowances, discounts, variable costs, capital needs, and dilution?

gates.label: 3 · Expectations
gates.detail: Do dated, fiscal-aligned estimate vintages and market prices omit the cash benefit?

priorityTests.title: AKAM · capacity to owner cash
priorityTests.observed: The September 24 8-K describes dedicated cloud capacity and about $11.6B of payments conditional on delivery, service availability, and termination terms. The first warrant tranche is not vested merely because the contract was signed.
priorityTests.missing: Full services and project-plan terms, delivered-capacity costs, financing, cash receipts, refresh needs, and realized dilution. The filing does not specify that the entire contract is CPU-only.
priorityTests.nextEvidence: September-quarter 10-Q exhibits, then deployment and project cash-flow disclosures against management's 2026–28 capex plan.

priorityTests.title: TWLO · paid usage to gross profit
priorityTests.observed: Twilio reported 49% FY2025 Voice AI customer-revenue growth from an undisclosed base and named multiple AI-related Q2 2026 customer wins. A vendor case reports more bookings, but not a controlled supplier-profit result.
priorityTests.missing: ConversationRelay-only paid minutes, realized net price, incremental carrier/speech cost, channel displacement, and matched net-new completed jobs.
priorityTests.nextEvidence: A paid Relay/Voice cohort with usage, revenue, gross profit, and completed outcomes versus comparable non-agent locations or customers.

priorityTests.title: AKAM + TWLO · expectation gap
priorityTests.observed: Company guidance and an attributed current Eulerpool snapshot can be displayed separately. Neither is a pre/post Street free-cash-flow revision history.
priorityTests.missing: Same-provider pre- and post-event FCF estimates for matching fiscal years, accounting definitions, valuation observations, and rights to retain or display that history.
priorityTests.nextEvidence: Secure permitted point-in-time history, then compare operating cash changes with the same fiscal-year estimate revisions and contemporaneous valuation.

workUnits.title: Resolve an inbound customer call
workUnits.path: Customer intent → voice session → retrieval → agent answer or handoff → completed appointment
workUnits.question: Did the agent recover a job that would otherwise be lost, and did the supplier earn more net cash?
workUnits.layers: Model inference · data access · communication · telemetry

workUnits.title: Change a business record
workUnits.path: User request → identity and policy → context retrieval → API write → audit trail
workUnits.question: Which checks and executions are separately paid, and which are bundled or cached?
workUnits.layers: Data access · APIs · identity · security · observability

workUnits.title: Complete a purchase or booking
workUnits.path: Discovery → comparison → authorization → payment or referral → fulfilled outcome
workUnits.question: Was the transaction incremental, or did an agent simply reroute an existing buyer?

layers.name: Inference and model mediation
layers.resource: Tokens, model calls, and orchestration time
layers.leakage: Smaller models, deterministic rules, caching, batching, and model-provider bundling
layers.evidenceNeeded: Production task share and net inference cash cost per completed outcome

layers.name: Physical compute and memory
layers.resource: CPU time, servers, memory, power, and colocation
layers.leakage: Build capex, power, depreciation, financing, buyer concentration, and refresh cycles
layers.evidenceNeeded: Contracted delivery, utilization, and lifecycle cash return

layers.name: Retrieval and data access
layers.resource: Search, indexing, context retrieval, and data movement
layers.possibleMeter: Paid executions, compute units, or data operations
layers.leakage: Included quotas, self-hosting, caching, and cheaper retrieval paths
layers.evidenceNeeded: Paid agent-attributed usage and realized contribution after hosting cost

layers.name: Network and APIs
layers.resource: Requests, tool calls, retries, and egress
layers.possibleMeter: Billable requests, CPU time, or bytes
layers.leakage: Internal APIs, low list prices, request consolidation, and free gateway tiers
layers.evidenceNeeded: Net paid usage per completed task, not raw bot traffic

layers.name: Identity, fraud, and security
layers.resource: Authorization, risk decisions, and protected legitimate API actions
layers.possibleMeter: Paid decisions or protected Good Requests
layers.leakage: Cached decisions, pooled entitlements, blocked traffic, and suite bundling
layers.evidenceNeeded: Agent-tagged paid volume, net yield, and incremental security gross profit

layers.name: Observability and audit
layers.possibleMeter: Billable retained spans or ingest volume
layers.leakage: Sampling, short retention, excluded tool spans, and open-source substitutes
layers.evidenceNeeded: Paid span mix and margin after data-processing cost

layers.name: Workflow and communication
layers.resource: Calls, messages, workflow steps, and human handoffs
layers.possibleMeter: Paid minutes, sends, or completed runs
layers.leakage: Shorter calls, direct APIs, channel displacement, and carrier or speech cost
layers.evidenceNeeded: Net new outcomes and supplier cash per completed job

layers.name: Transactions and referrals
layers.resource: Payments, orders, bookings, and closed referrals
layers.possibleMeter: Net processing spread or success fee
layers.leakage: Existing transactions rerouted through agents and take-rate compression
layers.evidenceNeeded: Controlled incremental completed outcomes and retained cash after partner fees

companies.name: Akamai
companies.paidUnit: Service payments after contracted capacity is delivered and available
companies.observed: $11.6B of conditional Anthropic payments for dedicated cloud capacity over seven-year project plans; management plans about $5.5B of related capex. The 8-K does not define this as CPU-only, and contract value is not recognized revenue.

materiality.note: Nominal capital recovery only; excludes discounting, replacement, financing, taxes, and warrant effects.

companies.cashUnknown: Full MSA terms, power and colocation economics, service cost, funding, refresh or residual value, and warrant-adjusted diluted shares. The first warrant tranche depends on a Project Plan 3 payment.
companies.breaker: Delivered capacity earns too little lifecycle owner cash after the build and warrant effects.
companies.nextTest: Read the full MSA and project plans when filed with the September-quarter 10-Q; reconcile payments, capex, cash returns, and pre/post-announcement fiscal-aligned estimates.
companies.expectations: No matched dated FCF-estimate revision panel; the announcement and price reaction alone do not prove mispricing.

companies.name: Twilio
companies.paidUnit: Relay list price of $0.07 per minute, with Voice billed separately
companies.observed: Twilio reports 49% FY2025 Voice AI customer-revenue growth from an undisclosed base and named Q2 2026 AI-related wins. A vendor-hosted Scorpion case reports 6,500 otherwise-missed appointments; none isolates incremental ConversationRelay gross profit.

materiality.unit: extra paid Relay minutes per year
materiality.note: List price and 50% incremental cash conversion are illustrative; realized yield and margin are undisclosed.

companies.cashUnknown: Incremental paid Relay minutes, net price, carrier and speech costs, and channel displacement.
companies.breaker: Agents complete more jobs but shorten calls, reroute customers to APIs, or replace existing paid channels.
companies.nextTest: Compare matched customer locations on total completed jobs, paid Voice/Relay minutes, and supplier gross profit.
companies.expectations: No agent-specific gross-profit or dated pre/post FCF consensus bridge.

companies.name: RELX Risk
companies.workUnit: Authorize an external transaction or account action
companies.paidUnit: Transaction-class or volume-linked contracts; a network event is not necessarily a new paid decision
companies.observed: 61% of FY2025 Risk revenue was transaction-class, including long-term volumetric contracts. Reported agentic traffic growth began from a tiny base.

materiality.note: £1 net fee and 60% incremental cash conversion are hypothetical, not RELX disclosed prices or margins.

companies.cashUnknown: Agent-tagged paid decision count, net fee, and cash contribution apart from ordinary fraud and digitalization.
companies.breaker: Credentials or decisions are reused, batched, or absorbed in existing volume commitments.
companies.nextTest: Find matched agent-exposed customer cohorts with paid decision volume and realized yield.
companies.expectations: No Risk-specific agent cash bridge or matched estimate vintages.

companies.name: F5
companies.workUnit: Inspect a legitimate agent API request
companies.paidUnit: Good Requests forwarded to origin, subject to contract terms and allowances
companies.observed: F5 defines the protected-request meter, but does not publish agent-specific paid volume or realized price per million.

materiality.basis: Nine months ended June 2026 CFO less PP&E
materiality.note: 60% incremental cash conversion is illustrative; the required revenue cannot be converted to requests without a net price.

companies.cashUnknown: Agent-classified Good Requests beyond included pools, realized price, and associated gross profit.
companies.breaker: New governance is bundled, blocked traffic does not bill, or optimized requests reduce paid usage.
companies.nextTest: Seek disclosed paid request growth and security revenue in matched agent-exposed accounts.
companies.expectations: No attributable revenue or dated estimate revision series.

companies.name: Jabil
companies.workUnit: Build servers for additional cloud capacity
companies.paidUnit: Recognized manufacturing sales and services, not Akamai's memory authorization
companies.observed: Akamai named Jabil in its build arrangements; the $1.7B customer-funded memory authorization is not disclosed Jabil revenue.

materiality.note: 3% incremental after-tax cash yield on truly new manufacturing sales is assumed, not company guidance.

companies.cashUnknown: Recognized contract sales, true program margin, inventory, tooling, receivable financing, and warranty costs.
companies.breaker: AI program sales replace other cloud builds or consume cash through working capital.
companies.nextTest: Reconcile Intelligent Infrastructure segment growth with cash conversion and customer-funded input accounting.
companies.expectations: AI infrastructure growth is already a public company narrative; no matched expectation gap.

companies.name: Elastic
companies.resource: Agent Builder execution and search compute
companies.paidUnit: Serverless completed execution after free allowances; other deployments may be bundled
companies.observed: Published Agent Builder starting price is $0.025 per completed execution after 1,000 free per project.

materiality.note: Starting list price and 60% incremental cash conversion are illustrative; discounts, free usage, and hosting cost matter.

companies.cashUnknown: Paid execution count by deployment, realized price, and incremental hosting margin.
companies.breaker: Execution growth is absorbed by free quotas, self-managed use, or enterprise bundles.
companies.nextTest: Seek paid serverless execution revenue and cash contribution separately from existing search workloads.
companies.expectations: AI positioning is overt; no dated attributable FCF revision panel.

companies.name: Zillow Preferred
companies.workUnit: Find a home and close a Zillow-sourced connection
companies.resource: Buyer intent, agent match, tour, and referral
companies.paidUnit: 15–40% of the agent commission on a closed Preferred transaction
companies.observed: The success-fee mechanism is disclosed, but no AI-originated incremental paid-close cohort is reported.

materiality.note: $10,000 commission and 30% incremental cash conversion are hypothetical; H1 FCF annualization ignores seasonality.

companies.cashUnknown: AI-attributed net-new Preferred closes and cash retained after incentives and model costs.
companies.breaker: Existing buyers move through Zillow Pro, competing listing-agent paths, or AI search without a new paid referral.
companies.nextTest: Compare AI and matched non-AI markets on new unrepresented-buyer connections, then collected close fees with a housing-cycle lag.
companies.expectations: No AI-paid-close disclosure or dated attribution in analyst FCF revisions.

methodology: The 5% hurdle is an illustrative materiality screen: 5% × the stated cash-flow baseline, with share count held constant. It is not a forecast, valuation, or price target.

Unit thresholds use the displayed list or hypothetical net price and assumed incremental cash conversion; actual realized yield, marginal cost, stock-based compensation, dilution, and capital needs may be different.
Periods and accounting definitions differ across companies. Do not compare the numerical hurdles as if they were normalized returns.

No candidate is marked underpriced until the same fiscal periods have dated pre/post estimates, valuation context, and attributable owner-cash evidence. Missing disclosure leaves a thesis unverified, not disproved.
